name: Niaz Mohammad Azad Shaik
tagline: QA and infrastructure engineer. I test networks, and I write about the failures that pass every check.

today.text: Alhamdulillah, my website went live today.

about: I'm a QA and infrastructure engineer at A10 Networks. Before that I worked at F5 Networks and Brocade Communications. Most of my career has gone into testing networking gear: load balancers, routers and switches, with DNS, sFlow and packet capture as my home ground. I hold an MS in Electrical Engineering.

Lately I have been carrying the same tester's habits into GPU and AI infrastructure. I measure what a GPU is really doing under load, check whether a retrieval system finds the right passage, and look for results that seem fine and are still wrong.
I write up what I find, including the parts that did not work.

articles.title: When Your DNS Tests Lie: Two Silent Failures Testing 49 Record Types
articles.about: An old dig quietly turned an unknown record type into two A queries, and the tests still passed.

articles.title: Did Every Collector Get Its Packets? A Checklist Approach to Verifying sFlow Export
articles.about: Capture the traffic, cross each expected collector off a list, and what is left is the failure report.

articles.title: Two Models, Two Checks, Opposite Rankings: Why Structural Validation Is Not Enough for Model Selection
articles.about: One model wrote perfect JSON with empty fields. The other wrote messy JSON with every answer right.

articles.title: GPU Utilization Says 100%. But What Is the GPU Actually Doing?
articles.about: A T4 pinned at its 70 W power cap, with the clock well below boost the whole time.

articles.title: GPU Under Load, Part 2
articles.about: Two workloads with the same power and utilization, and a twofold difference in clock speed.

articles.title: GPU Metrics and Cloud Limits
articles.about: What happened when I tried DCGM on Colab, and why it needs a real GPU node.

articles.title: RAG Retrieval Evaluation
articles.about: Every obvious fix was ambiguous until measured, and the best method looked worst at first.

articles.title: RAG Generation Faithfulness
articles.about: Whether a model sticks to its context depends on the passage it is given, not the question.

articles.title: CUDA Silent Failure
articles.about: A wrong launch size left 744 elements unwritten, with no crash and no error to catch.
